hints: Substitute $x = 4$ into the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} = 4(2x - 5)^3 - 9x^{1/2}$ to find the gradient of the tangent at $A$.
Use the perpendicular gradient relationship $m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{tangent}}}$ to find the gradient of the normal.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the gradient of the curve (tangent) at $A\left(4, -\frac{11}{2}\right)$ by substituting $x = 4$ into $\frac{dy}{dx}$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=4} = 4(2(4) - 5)^3 - 9(4)^{1/2} = 4(3)^3 - 9(2) = 4(27) - 18 = 108 - 18 = 90$$

Since the normal is perpendicular to the tangent ($m_{\text{normal}} \times m_{\text{tangent}} = -1$), calculate the normal gradient:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{90} \approx -0.0111$$

hints: Integrate the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} = 4(2x - 5)^3 - 9x^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$ to find $y$, remembering the constant of integration $+c$.
Use the reverse chain rule on $4(2x - 5)^3$: $\int 4(2x-5)^3 dx = 4 \times \frac{(2x-5)^4}{4 \times 2} = \frac{1}{2}(2x-5)^4$.
Substitute the coordinates of point $A\left(4, -\frac{11}{2}\right)$ to solve for $c$ and state the full equation of the curve.
walkthrough:
Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 4(2x-5)^3 - 9x^{1/2}$ term-by-term with respect to $x$:
$$\int 4(2x - 5)^3 dx = 4 \times \frac{(2x - 5)^4}{4 \times 2} = \frac{1}{2}(2x - 5)^4$$
$$\int 9x^{1/2} dx = 9 \times \frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} = 9 \times \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2} = 6x^{3/2}$$

Combine terms and include the constant of integration $c$:
$$y = \frac{1}{2}(2x - 5)^4 - 6x^{3/2} + c$$

Substitute the given point $A\left(4, -\frac{11}{2}\right)$ into the curve equation to find $c$:
$$-\frac{11}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(2(4) - 5)^4 - 6(4)^{3/2} + c \implies -\frac{11}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(81) - 6(8) + c$$
$$-\frac{11}{2} = \frac{81}{2} - 48 + c = -\frac{15}{2} + c \implies c = -\frac{11}{2} + \frac{15}{2} = 2$$

State the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = \frac{1}{2}(2x - 5)^4 - 6x^{3/2} + 2$$
